title: kovee-mcp tool-schema document (C3a)
description: Closed meta-schema for mcp/kovee-mcp.tools.json — the versioned MCP tool bundle binding the C3a sheet's kovee-mcp participant profile (../plan/sheets/C3a.md) onto the K0-frozen registry's operation names (spec/registry.json). Tool names are a closed enum of exactly 14, so a worker- or operator-surface operation as a tool name fails this schema (deny-by-absence); the profiles object is itself closed — exactly one participant profile, no candidate/worker/operator profile can exist. The sheet_ops const pins every sheet-name-to-registry-name mapping (relation_add binds relation_assert; artifact_upload expands to the registry's five-operation upload flow). Per-tool input schemas are derived from the spec/schemas/ops request args minus the channel-derived fields; the field-subset, access, and registry-surface rules JSON Schema cannot express are enforced by mcp/check.py (standalone; runner wiring deferred).

version.description: Version of this tool-schema document (a lock-manifest row per the C3a sheet).

kcp_protocol_version.description: The KCP major.minor version whose op schemas these tools bind (§11; initial version 0.1).

source.description: Provenance pins: the closed op list comes from the C3a sheet (family plan repository, sibling checkout), the operation names and surfaces from the K0-frozen registry, the input schemas from the committed op request schemas.

sheet_ops.description: The recorded sheet-name-to-registry-name mapping, const-pinned: the C3a sheet's ten kovee-mcp ops in sheet order, each mapped to the registry operation(s) that realize it. relation_add is the sheet's name for the registry's relation_assert; artifact_upload names the §10.10 upload flow, which the registry decomposes into begin/show/credential/finalize/abort (registry order); every other sheet name is also the registry name. No sheet op is without a registry counterpart.

profiles.description: Exactly the one C3a kovee-mcp profile; closed — no candidate, worker, operator, or any other profile exists.

assertion.const: No worker- or operator-surface operation is bound as a tool, ever.

excluded_surfaces.description: The deny-by-absence assertion (C3a sheet: participant-scoped KCP rows only). The closed tool-name enum makes it structural; this records it in the document itself, and mcp/check.py re-derives it against the registry's per-surface rows.

participantToolName.description: The exact participant-profile tool set: the C3a sheet's ten kovee-mcp ops in sheet order under the sheet_ops mapping (artifact_upload expanded to the registry's five upload operations). external_client surface only.

sheetOpName.description: The C3a sheet's kovee-mcp op names, verbatim (closed).

participantBinding.description: The participant-scoped binding envelope: an authenticated participant channel on the external_client surface only — no worker or operator row is reachable through it. The channel pins realm_id and project_id (§11.2 envelope scoping), so they are never tool arguments; elicitation through the binding is never assent.

op.description: The registry operation this tool binds; name must equal kovee_<op> (check-enforced).

sheet_op.description: The C3a sheet name this tool realizes — the per-tool record of the sheet_ops mapping (check-enforced against it).

op_request_schema.description: The committed spec/schemas/ops request schema the input schema derives from. Never null: all ten mapped registry operations have committed K0 request schemas.

access.description: The akson-mcp marking: read-only tools are safe to allow; authority-bearing tools stay gated so each call is a deliberate yes. Mutations (meta-requiring ops) are gated; reads are safe to allow except the credential-minting artifact_upload_credential read, which stays gated (check-enforced).

inputSchema.description: A closed embedded JSON Schema: the op request `args` object minus channel-derived fields. The envelope {version, op, meta, realm_id, project_id, ext} never appears (the bridge derives protocol version from negotiation, meta and realm/project scope from the participant channel), and neither do the worker-binding args {attempt_id, fence_epoch} (KG14: forbidden on external_client) nor the events_read args-level project_id (the binding pins the project scope). additionalProperties false is mandatory — an input carrying an undeclared or channel-derived field fails the tool call.
